limitations: Body receipt availability is an upper bound on potentially available inputs.
The computation time of the reconstructed owner/signer/buyer features is unknown; receipt does not prove a strategy had those features.
The 77 paper rows share 39 signal keys; correlated variants are not independent observations or real executions.
Saved histories are incomplete and selected after observation. Zero retained records does not prove no prior activity.
This audit tests neither independence, PnL, prediction, strategy eligibility nor profitability.
The seven-wallet RPC history is separate from the recorder archive; zero contemporaneous archive coverage remains unchanged.

match_criteria.availability: earliest valid received_at_utc across successful finalized bodies in seven pinned retained RPC files; must equal normalized available_at_utc; missing or invalid candidate times remain unknown
match_criteria.dedup_key: event_id = signature:event:complete-event-bytes-sha256:occurrence; identical IDs counted once; conflicting IDs fail
match_criteria.entry_cutoff: UTC timestamp of trade.entry_at; inclusive event_time <= cutoff AND receipt_time <= cutoff
match_criteria.paper_rows: trade.meta.mint equals target exactly; no symbol or pool-valued asset substitution
match_criteria.prior_for_selected_buy: same wallet, event_time strictly before selected buy; receipt_time <= selected buy event time
match_criteria.signal_cutoff: UTC timestamp of trade.meta.signal_t; inclusive event_time <= cutoff AND receipt_time <= cutoff
match_criteria.target_buy_event: normalized mint equals target exactly, side equals buy, transaction-user signer proof true, and matching saved finalized getTransaction body with explicit meta.err null and primary signature equal requested signature
match_criteria.timestamp_policy: ISO timestamps must be timezone-aware; epoch timestamps must be finite numeric non-booleans; invalid, missing, inconsistent timestamps stay null/unknown, never converted to zero

question: Which pinned Claudia paper decisions had target-buy transaction bodies received before signal or entry rather than merely earlier event times?
result: Timing evidence can expose look-ahead and coverage limits; it cannot validate a buyer-conditioned strategy or establish eligibility.
